name: Gas-to-methanol and methanol-to-gasoline
principle: Natural gas is reformed to synthesis gas, which is converted to methanol over a copper catalyst in a synthesis loop. Methanol-to-gasoline (ExxonMobil MTG) then converts methanol to gasoline-range hydrocarbons over a zeolite. A 2017 comparison of three natural-gas routes found large exergetic differences between a plain steam-methane-reforming plant and combined reforming.

process_steps.name: Reforming to syngas (SMR, SMR plus ATR or CO2 reforming)

performance.basis: Case I SMR 28.2% (2,200 t/d); Case III CO2 plus steam reforming 41.0%; Case II SMR+ATR 55.6%; paper's simulation, not plant data

source.note: Blumberg, Morosuk and Tsatsaronis, A Comparative Exergoeconomic Evaluation of the Synthesis Routes for Methanol Production from Natural Gas, Applied Sciences 7(12), 1213 (2017)

advantages: Large plants with combined reforming are competitive (study)
limitations: The study calls the plain SMR case hardly economically feasible

sources.note: Blumberg, Morosuk and Tsatsaronis, A Comparative Exergoeconomic Evaluation of the Synthesis Routes for Methanol Production from Natural Gas, Applied Sciences 7(12), 1213 (2017)
